title: CA-CRS+: A Zone-Aware, Resource-Informed Crowd Risk Scoring Framework with Cause-Specific Gate Intervention Recommendation for Stampede Prevention
description:
CA-CRS+ is an edge-deployable, RGB-only crowd safety framework designed to detect impending stampedes and crush conditions, attribute the underlying causal driver (Density, Speed, or Conflict), actuate named gate interventions with ripple-effect prevention, and size medical/security personnel demand dynamically.

Key Contributions & Findings:

  • Benchmark-Validated Counting: Replaces whole-body detection with density-map regression (DM-Count VGG-19; validated at MAE 48.7 on ShanghaiTech Part A, MAE 14.4 on Part B, and MAE 0.55 against multi-object-tracking ground truth on PETS2009 S2.L1).
  • Circular-Variance Conflict Index: Normalized directional conflict metric via magnitude-weighted circular variance of optical flow that does not degenerate under balanced counter-flow.
  • Non-Linear Crush Scoring: Solves the zero-velocity gridlock paradox where dense stationary crowds are scored as safe by linear models. On dense imagery, CA-CRS+ flags 55% of scenes as DANGER where a matched linear baseline flags 0%.
  • Cause-to-Gate Mapping with Ripple-Effect Downgrade: Emits named gate commands (Density → OPEN, Speed → CLOSE, Conflict → REDIRECT, MIXED → HOLD) with a safety check preventing crowd redirection from overwhelming downstream zones.
  • Dynamic Resource-Aware Alerting: Sizes marshal demand logarithmically with crowd population (D_mar = ceil(alpha * log10(1 + N))).
  • Multi-Camera Fusion: Fuses multiple real CCTV camera streams into an urgency-weighted (2:1) Global Risk Score (GRS).
  • Edge Performance: Runs at 4.0 frames/s on a single commodity NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPU, supporting real-time 1–2 Hz risk-update cadences.

Note: This research work was originally prepared for IEEE TENCON 2026, withdrawn by the authors after peer-review revisions, and is released here as an open-access research preprint and reproducible artifact archive with source code, benchmark data, and verification scripts.
